sections.title: Stallholder Application
sections.context: A man named Tom is inquiring about renting a stall at the local farmers' market from the market organizer, Mrs. Higgins.

transcript.speaker: Mrs. Higgins
transcript.text: Good morning, Riverside Farmers' Market office. Sarah Higgins speaking. How can I help you?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Hello, Sarah. My name is Tom and I’m calling to inquire about getting a stall at your market. I’ve heard it’s quite popular.

transcript.speaker: Mrs. Higgins
transcript.text: It certainly is! We have a long waiting list for some categories, but we're always looking for high-quality local produce. What is your full name, please?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: It’s Tom Weston. That’s W-E-S-T-O-N.

transcript.speaker: Mrs. Higgins
transcript.text: Thank you, Tom. And what exactly is it that you produce on your farm?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I specialize in organic honey. I’ve got about fifty hives now. I also make a few beeswax candles, but the main thing is the honey.

transcript.speaker: Mrs. Higgins
transcript.text: Organic honey, that’s wonderful. We actually don't have a dedicated honey stall at the moment. Now, what size stall would you require? Our standard units are three meters or two meters.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Well, I originally thought I’d need the three-meter one to fit all my display jars, but looking at my transport van, I think a 2 meters space will be enough for me. Yes, let's go with the smaller one.

transcript.speaker: Mrs. Higgins
transcript.text: Right, a two-meter stall. And which market days are you interested in? We run on Wednesdays and Saturdays.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Wednesday is difficult because I have deliveries to local shops then. So Saturday is definitely the best option for me.

transcript.speaker: Mrs. Higgins
transcript.text: Perfect. Now, do you have any specific requirements for your setup? Some vendors need water access or refrigeration.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I don't need water, but I will need electricity. I have some digital scales and a small display light that I'd like to use if it's a cloudy day.

transcript.speaker: Mrs. Higgins
transcript.text: That can be arranged. Now, let's go over some of the formal requirements and costs. First, all our stallholders must hold valid public liability insurance. Do you have that?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yes, I've got a policy that covers up to five million dollars.

transcript.speaker: Mrs. Higgins
transcript.text: Excellent. Regarding the costs, the weekly fee for a two-meter stall on a Saturday is 45 pounds. It’s slightly cheaper on Wednesdays, but as you said, Saturdays are busier.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Forty-five pounds sounds reasonable. When would I need to arrive to set up?

transcript.speaker: Mrs. Higgins
transcript.text: The market opens to the public at 8:00 AM, so we require all vendors to arrive by 6:30 AM at the latest. If you're not there by then, we might give your spot to someone on the casual list.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I see. I'll make sure to set my alarm early! Where should I park my van?

transcript.speaker: Mrs. Higgins
transcript.text: You should enter through the South Gate. There’s a designated area for stallholders' vehicles right behind the main square.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: South Gate, got it. Any other rules I should know about?

transcript.speaker: Mrs. Higgins
transcript.text: Just one major one regarding the environment. We are a plastic-free market. You must ensure you take home all packaging that you bring. We don't allow any cardboard or plastic to be left in the site bins.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: That's no problem at all. I use glass jars and paper bags anyway. Thanks for the information, Sarah.

transcript.speaker: Mrs. Higgins
transcript.text: You're welcome, Tom. I'll email you the application form now.
